SAP HANA and HANA Cloud

Source: vignettes/hana.Rmd
hana.Rmd

SAP HANA is a SQL database available on your own infrastructure or through HANA Cloud. shinyOAuthDB lets a Shiny app query it using each visitor’s account, so HANA’s database privileges control what the app can read.

oauth_db_hana() opens a DBI connection for SQL or dbplyr. Your sign-in provider issues a signed access token, and HANA maps that token’s identity to a database user. The example first shows that user so you can check the connection before querying a table.

Before running the app

Install odbc in R and SAP HANA Client’s ODBC driver for your R architecture. Use odbc::odbcListDrivers() to find its registered name, commonly HDBODBC.

Ask your administrator to configure HANA to accept signed JWT access tokens and map them to database users. You need these settings:

Setting Where to find it
Server and SQL port HANA connection details; HANA Cloud normally uses port 443
Tenant database, if needed Self-hosted HANA connection details
OAuth issuer The sign-in service HANA trusts
Client ID and secret Your OAuth application registration
Access scope and audience The provider configuration agreed with the HANA administrator
TLS trust store, if needed The certificate chain required by your HANA Client

Register http://localhost:8100 as the redirect URI. The example uses a provider with OpenID Connect and refresh tokens. Its database.read scope is a placeholder: ask your administrator to define or replace it, and configure the token audience for this database.

Save the settings in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-shiny-app-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-shiny-app-client-secret
OAUTHDB_HANA_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
OAUTHDB_HANA_SCOPE=database.read
OAUTHDB_HANA_SERVER=your-instance.hana.prod-eu10.hanacloud.ondemand.com
OAUTHDB_HANA_PORT=443
OAUTHDB_HANA_DRIVER=HDBODBC

A complete app

This app displays the database user HANA assigned to the visitor. Replace the query with a table or view the signed-in user can read.

After signing in, click Load rows. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

pkgs <- c("shiny", "shinyOAuth", "shinyOAuthDB", "mirai", "odbc")
for (pkg in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

scope <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_SCOPE")

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_ISSUER")
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "offline_access", scope),
  required_scopes = scope
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())
  con <- oauth_db_hana(
    auth$connection,
    server = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_SERVER"),
    port = as.integer(Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_PORT", "443")),
    driver = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_DRIVER", "HDBODBC"),
    required_scopes = scope
  )
  query_task <- oauth_db_task(con)
  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke("SELECT CURRENT_USER AS DATABASE_USER FROM DUMMY")
  })
  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)
    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.

Save the app as example.R and run source("example.R"). Open http://localhost:8100 in a regular browser; embedded IDE viewers cannot complete the OAuth redirects.

For a self-hosted tenant, set its SQL port and add database = "REPORTING" when required by the connection details. Use schema = "SALES" to select an initial schema. Set ssl_trust_store if the client’s configured trust store does not contain the server’s certificate chain. The helper always requires encryption, certificate validation and the endpoint’s hostname.

Configure HANA’s JWT provider

The database needs a JWT provider, trusted signing certificates and a mapping from external identities to database users. Grant those users access to the tables your app will query. Follow SAP’s JWT configuration procedure for HANA Platform, or the corresponding procedure for your HANA Cloud release.

The app must obtain a JWT access token with the expected issuer, audience and identity claims. Signing in to SAP BTP or another SAP application doesn’t by itself establish a HANA SQL identity. This guide queries the HANA database; SAP application APIs and the HANA Cloud data lake engine have separate setups.

Connection lifetime

Call connection <- con() before each operation. A valid SQL connection stays open through ordinary token renewal, with the identity and privileges established when it connected. Sign-out, account changes or the end of the Shiny session close it.

If the connection breaks, the next con() opens a new one with a current token. The helper doesn’t replay a failed query. See ?oauth_db_hana for connection settings and SAP’s HANA Cloud ODBC guide for driver setup.
